enumeration.method: Independent small-cap-heading enumeration and visual comparison of all seven complete Theorems.

checks: Seven printed Theorems in the main text are retained in full, including the classical Theorem 4.1. Small-cap theorem headings were independently enumerated on pages 1 through the main-text prefix of page 29; appendix bodies are excluded.

Fifteen entries and fourteen supporting passages preserve the author kernel/privacy conventions, DQM and Fisher information, LAMN, fixed-channel MLE, hard truncation, separate C1-C3, full consistent quantizer, finite channel matrix domain and the complete six-step estimator.

Independent reconstruction gives 31 direct uses and 41 related connections. Theorem 4.1 retains no ranked direct dependencies because its raw-model and likelihood quantities are ambient or locally bound. Theorem 3.5 imports only the information definition from Theorem 3.3, not its LAMN conclusion. Theorem 4.3 has no DQM assumption.

Theorem 3.3 uses weak convergence and allows singular limiting information; Theorem 3.5 requires positivity at finite n and at every weak accumulation point. C1-C3 remain distinct. The quantizer error vanishes along every convergent parameter sequence, not only pointwise.

Private MLEs preserve their exact likelihood and measurable-maximizer requirements. Hard truncation is zero outside the l1 ball. The two-step estimator retains all six steps, conditional pmfs, n2 normalization and arbitrary fallback; Theorem 4.12 assumes consistency and uses sqrt(n) local-alternative scaling.

Eight scope/convention issues are recorded separately. The noisy moment mean need not lie in the stated inverse domain; Theorem 4.11 prints a nonnegative difference at different parameters; the bounded set in Lemma 4.5 is called a cone. Source statements are preserved without correction or proof certification.

Every entry has literal author terminology, faithful source-kind labels and meaningful matching selectors. DQM is the source acronym for C1; the original Definition 1 and assumptions are retained separately. All 41 theorem relations have source-specific paths and explanations.

All six content JSON files reproduce byte for byte from the retained per-paper scripts. Independent source-specific checks, graph reconstruction, inventory validation and frozen hashes protect the reviewed extraction; rebuilding alone is not a new source review.

source_notes.description: The author writes Z^(0)=emptyset=G^(0) and A times emptyset=A as a formal convention. This is not literal Cartesian-product set theory; preserve the printed convention and flag it for later formalization.

Q_alpha(X) is a union over all measurable output spaces. Footnote 1 explicitly replaces scalar Fisher supremum notation by a supremum over attainable real numbers; the census retains that explanation.

Theorem 4.3 applies f^{-1}:G->Theta to the noisy mean of Z_i, but no extension or fallback outside G is given. The noisy mean need not belong to G. Preserve the theorem as printed; its domain issue is not solved by the census.

Theorem 4.11 prints 0 <= sup_Q I_theta(QP)-I_theta_n1(Qhat That P) for arbitrary theta and theta_n1. Comparing information at different parameters does not by itself justify nonnegativity. Preserve the printed bound and flag its scope; the census does not certify or correct the claim.

Lemma 4.5 calls C_alpha(k) a convex cone while imposing 0<=v_j<=1. The upper bound prevents closure under arbitrary positive scaling. Preserve the set and original wording, without dropping its upper bound.
The fixed-channel MLE definition invokes q(z|x) from Lemma D.2. Its main-text integrated density and bounds are retained; the appendix lemma is not inspected or imported.

Theorems 4.1 and 4.2 retain the event estimator in compact K in their convergence statements. They do not by themselves assert unrestricted consistency without an additional tightness or compact-parameter argument.

Theorem 4.12 explicitly assumes consistency of the second-stage MLE. The procedure allows an arbitrary value when no maximizer exists. Neither consistency nor universal attainment is inferred from the efficiency conclusion.

ambient_resolution.T3.3: Q^(n), its conditional kernels and experiment law resolve through D1-D3; DQM and score/information through D5-D6. Sigma and Delta are locally defined, with Sigma retained in A6 for the next theorem. D7 and A4 define the LAMN conclusion. Countable generation, nonzero original information and weak convergence are explicit hypotheses. The limit need not be positive definite. A5 fixes identity J_p and weak convergence.
ambient_resolution.T3.5: D1-D3 define the experiment. D5-D6 and A6 resolve averaged conditional information. All finite-n information matrices and every weak accumulation point are assumed positive definite. The regular estimator/local-alternative limit D_theta, Gaussian convolution kernel and mixture representation are locally bound. No full-sequence LAMN assumption or conclusion is imported from Theorem 3.3.
ambient_resolution.T4.1: A7 supplies the dominated raw-data model, and A5 its density/expectation conventions. Every likelihood, supremum, compact set and maximizer is bound in the theorem. Thus its ranked direct-interface list is empty without omitting the theorem. No private channel, DQM, Section 4 scalar restriction or two-stage estimator is imposed on this classical multivariate statement.
ambient_resolution.T4.2: D1-D2 resolve QP, D5 with A3 resolves DQM at every parameter, and D8 defines the non-interactive private MLE including the integrated density and maximization. Identifiability is the ambient injectivity of theta->QP_theta, explicitly assumed. Compact-intersection convergence is retained; the classical Theorem 4.1 is a proof reference.
ambient_resolution.T4.3: D9 supplies the hard l1-ball truncation; D4 defines the non-interactive privacy conclusion. g, its range G, f=E_theta g, the inverse, independent iid-component Laplace noise, Z_i, the estimator and both growth conditions are all bound in the theorem under the dominated model A7. The inverse-outside-G issue is retained separately. No DQM is assumed and no preliminary root-n rate is inferred.
ambient_resolution.T4.11: C1-C3 resolve independently to D10-D12; D13 retains the full Definition 3 including Delta and convergence along arbitrary convergent parameters. D14 is the finite channel matrix domain, D1-D2 the kernel/privacy convention and D6 Fisher information. A9 defines the cited measurable-maximizer sense; A10 supplies phi; A2 the unrestricted scalar supremum. Q0, n1, the preliminary estimator, its plugged-in quantizer/alphabet, theta_n1, C_alpha and the consistency condition are theorem-local. The cross-parameter 0<= statement remains a source issue.
ambient_resolution.T4.12: C1-C3 are D10-D12. D15 preserves every step of the estimator/experiment, with D3 and A12-A13 giving the sequential protocol and conditional iid second group. D1-D2,D6 and A2 resolve I*_alpha,theta0. Three density derivatives and their L1 regularity are explicit local assumptions, with the scalar parameter, positive information, n1->infinity, n1/n->0, consistency at theta0 and local h all retained. The final rate is sqrt(n); a root-n first-stage rate is not required.

source_claim_references.scope: Only the displayed Sigma_n,theta definition is imported, retained as A6; no full-sequence weak convergence or LAMN assumption is added.
The proof verifies classical likelihood conditions for private densities. Theorem 4.2 does not assume those conditions independently.
Main-text statements retained in A9 and A10 specify the measurable selection and error modulus actually named in the theorem.
Approximation and finite-output reduction are proof machinery, not additional hypotheses/definitions of the theorem estimator.
D15 and A12-A13 retain the estimator and full sample distribution explicitly imported by the theorem.
Referenced via private MLE D8. Preserve the main-text density formula and reference; do not read the appendix.

review_limits: Registered arXiv v3 manuscript identified by version and hash; no claim of byte-equivalence to the final journal article.
Original source conventions and ambiguities are retained separately; no appendix material is used in the census.
Source and schema validation do not certify mathematical proofs.
